title: metrics
summary: Size and complexity rows from the index per routine, class, unit and folder, with repeated parameter groups, single implementors, and a saved trend between index runs
intro: Read this when you want numbers about a codebase instead of findings: where the complexity sits, how big each unit and folder is, how coupled they are, which parameter lists repeat and which interfaces have a single implementor. Every number is read from the index; nothing is estimated, and --save / --trend show how the numbers moved between two index runs.

help: drag-lint metrics            --db <db> [--level routine,class,unit,folder|all] [--in <path prefix>] [--top <n>] [--save] [--trend] [--json]
size and complexity rows from the index (read-only): a total, then folders, units, classes and
routines with cyclomatic (sum / max), routines, body_loc, lines, comment lines, params, fan_in, fan_out.
fan: routine = distinct callers / callees; class = heirs in the index / declared ancestors;
unit = units using it / units it uses; folder = the same across the folder boundary.
A folder row covers the units directly in it. Nothing is estimated: a routine without stored facts has no row.
Then two sections: repeated parameter groups (3+ parameters shared by 3+ differently named routines)
and one implementor / one descendant (interfaces and classes with exactly one heir inside this index).
Text shows the --top rows (default 20, 0 = all) with the highest cyclomatic value; --json is never cut.
--level picks the row tables; --in keeps the files under a path (fan still counted over the index).
--save appends a snapshot (total + unit rows) to <db>.metrics.jsonl beside the index; the index is not written.
--trend compares the last two snapshots: total deltas, and each unit added / removed / changed.
--trend with fewer than two snapshots is refused and says how many the file holds. --save --trend = save, then compare.
json: schema "metrics/1", db, indexed_at_unix, total{row}, folders[], units[], classes[], routines[] (row = level, name,
parent, kind, file, line, symbol_id, nested, units, classes, interfaces, routines, cyclomatic, cyclomatic_max, body_loc,
body_loc_max, lines, comment_lines, params, fan_in, fan_out; null fan = not measured),
param_groups[{params[], routines[{name, file, line}]}], single_heirs[{kind, name, file, line, heir, heir_file, heir_line}].
--trend --json: schema "metrics-trend/1", snapshots, from, to, total{number: {from, to, delta}},
units[{status added|removed|changed, name, file, numbers}], units_unchanged.
Exit 0 = answered; 1 = history file unreadable / not writable; 2 = no --db, missing or unreadable index,
unknown --level, --save/--trend with --in, --trend with fewer than two snapshots; 3 = unknown flag.

questions.ask: Which routines are the most complex in this project?
How big and how coupled is each unit and folder?
Which parameter lists repeat across routines, and which interfaces have one implementor?
Did complexity go up since the last index run?
